name: The Lumen Climb
description: Every year on the first Saturday of May, residents across all tiers of GLMZ take part in the Lumen Climb — a tradition in which people physically ascend as high as they can reach by midnight and illuminate something: a candle, a glow-mod, a bioluminescent geneware pulse, a drone light, a BCI-projected halo, whatever they have. The tradition began in 2211 when a spontaneous Shelf rooftop vigil for a beloved community artist named Cass Ferundez-Okoro spread virally across the city through BCI-shared footage, with people at every tier stepping outside and adding their own light to the skyline.
cultural_impact: The Lumen Climb is the only tradition in M88 that genuinely crosses all tier boundaries without corporate engineering — watching the city light up from Shelf rooftops to Spire balconies on the same night carries an emotional weight that even jaded residents describe as the closest thing to civic unity the city has.
key_figures: Cass Ferundez-Okoro (artist whose death inspired the first climb, deceased 2211)
Yara Nkemdirim-Solis (the BCI broadcaster who spread the original footage)
The Altitude Collective (annual rooftop event organizers, Tier 2)
locations: The Climb Route, a mapped vertical path through Tiers 1-3
Spire Observation Ring, Tier 5 (contested — Spire residents didn't start participating until 2216)
story_hooks: Helix Media has quietly been purchasing the naming rights to 'The Lumen Climb' and plans to announce a rebranded corporate sponsorship this year — the Altitude Collective has forty-eight hours to decide whether to fight it, accept it, or do something drastic enough to make the tradition legally uncapturable.

A Shelf resident with no geneware, no BCI, and no tech climbs to the highest accessible point in their district every year with a single match — this year, someone in the Spire saw their tiny flame and wants to find them, for reasons that may not be benign.

Cass Ferundez-Okoro's death in 2211 was ruled an accident, but a recently surfaced piece of their final artwork contains what looks like a coded message suggesting they knew they were in danger — and the person they were afraid of is still prominent in M88's art world.
origin_event: The death of beloved Shelf artist Cass Ferundez-Okoro on April 29, 2211, and the spontaneous rooftop vigil held by their Shelf community that spread via BCI broadcast across the city, prompting people at every tier to step outside and add their own light to the skyline in an unplanned, city-wide act of shared grief.
tier_observations: Tier 1 observes with rooftop gatherings, communal fires, and geneware light shows — the Ferundez-Okoro Rooftop in District 6 is a pilgrimage site. Tier 2 climbs fire escapes, water towers, and elevated transit lines, mixing celebration with the tradition's grief roots. Tier 3 organizes building rooftop parties that are equal parts memorial and social event. Tier 4 hosts drone-light displays from corporate tower terraces that are spectacular but feel disconnected from the tradition's origin. Tier 5 Spire residents began participating only in 2216, largely through BCI-projected halos and bioluminescent geneware pulses from balconies — some Shelf residents resent the Spire's adoption of the tradition as appropriation; others see it as the point.
